ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Synthesis and Inquiry: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the quadratic function $y=x^2+bx+c$ passes through point $A\left(0, -\frac{7}{4}\right)$ and point $B\left(1, \frac{1}{4}\right)$. What is the analytical expression of this quadratic function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substitute $A\left(0, -\frac{7}{4}\right)$ and point $B\left(1, \frac{1}{4}\right)$ into $y=x^{2}+bx+c$ to get: \\
\[
\begin{cases}
-\frac{7}{4}=c\\
\frac{1}{4}=1+b+c
\end{cases}
,\] solving this system of equations gives
\[
\begin{cases}
b=1\\
c=-\frac{7}{4}
\end{cases},
\]
$\therefore y=x^{2}+x-\frac{7}{4}$. Therefore, the quadratic function is $\boxed{y=x^{2}+x-\frac{7}{4}}$.
